acceptance: cargo fmt --all -- --check passes on the exact implementation head.
cargo check --workspace --all-targets --offline passes on the exact implementation head.
cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --offline -- -D warnings passes on the exact implementation head.
cargo test --workspace --all-targets --offline passes on the exact implementation head.
cargo metadata --no-deps --format-version 1 identifies only the intended first-party workspace member, and dependency evidence confirms no third-party runtime or build dependency was admitted.
The checked-in .diffcipline.toml is valid against the pinned Diffcipline implementation and references only verification commands that exist in this Grain.
GitHub Actions runs the verification contract on Ubuntu, macOS, and Windows and the exact implementation head passes every required matrix job before acceptance.
The implementation adds no memory-domain behavior and changes no path outside the declared Grain change surface.

minimality.rationale: A minimal native Cargo workspace and first-party crate are the smallest executable foundation. No third-party runtime dependency or donor code is needed for this tooling-only Grain.

outcome: Morize has a dependency-free minimal Rust workspace with one first-party core crate, real local verification commands, a checked-in Diffcipline policy, and cross-platform CI, without implementing memory-domain behavior.
rationale: This bounded child establishes only the executable repository/tooling foundation required before deterministic domain contracts can be implemented. It intentionally excludes memory types, persistence, policy, retrieval, APIs, models, vectors, graphs, and managed infrastructure.

risk.recovery: Revert the bounded workspace/tooling commit set; no user data, persistent format, public API, or runtime state exists in this Grain.

scope_in: Create a root Cargo workspace and one minimal first-party morize-core library crate with no third-party runtime dependencies.
Establish real offline formatting, static-analysis, build/check, and test commands for the workspace.
Check in a real .diffcipline.toml bound to commands that exist in the new workspace.
Add a GitHub Actions matrix for Ubuntu, macOS, and Windows that executes the same verification contract.
Document the exact developer verification commands in CONTRIBUTING.md.
scope_out: Stable identities, digests, domain memory types, serialization formats, configuration semantics, and public error taxonomy.
Vault, persistence, migrations, recovery, policy, privacy, retrieval, APIs, MCP, models, vectors, graph systems, UI, team mode, and managed services.
Release packaging, publishing, benchmarks, and feature-rich runtime behavior.
title: Establish minimal Rust workspace and verification spine
